messages.author: ca0f657287afb1ff
messages.subject: create_mats
parts:
Hi Chris,
I would like to creat matrix for deterministic structural network using the code in the manual of BrainGraph 2.7.0 with threshold.by='consensus' and thresholds=seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.1). 
1. If meanFA matrix were selected, I can see the matrix in A.norm.sub changes at different thresholds by using corrplot. However, for most subjects, the matrix contains no edges at thresholds=>0.7. Is that normal?
2. If FiberNumber matrix were selected, the matrix presents no changes at different thresholds. I don't think that is normal. Could you help me out?

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] create_mats
parts:
Hi,
When you say you have "thresholds=seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.1)", is this what you provide to the argument "mat.thresh"? Because that is the appropriate way to do so.

1. Could you tell me what you mean by "meanFA matrix"? I assume you mean that the input matrix entries represent the mean FA along the tract. If that is the case, I would not expect there to be 0 edges that remain with a threshold of 0.7. Are you using the default "sub.thresh=0.5"? It could be that less than 1/2 of your subjects have a mean FA of 0.7 for those tracts. How many subjects do you have, and what is the variability in FA across subjects?
2. For fiber number, you will have to change the thresholds to be integer values. For example, "thresholds=seq(1, 10, 1)".

Chris

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] create_mats
parts:
I have looked at your data.

1. For the mean FA matrices, the maximum across all subjects is actually 0.69; this is why setting a threshold = 0.7 results in 0 edges. (I ran "apply(my.mats$A, 3, max)"). I am not sure why that is the case, but perhaps there is a lot of variability in your FA data. You should check what some of the "tracts" look like, and check to see if the "tracts" are properly defined. If, for example, they pass through a lot of gray matter, that would be the cause of a lower average FA along the tract.
2. For your error when trying to normalize by "size", that means that it cannot find the files specified by "div.files". So you can first try "sapply(matfiles$nodeVolumn, file.exists)" to see if they have the correct path.
3. For your "FiberNumber2", it looks like all of the matrices have different edge counts; i.e., I don't see what the error is in that case.
4. RE your question about symmetrizing using "avg": I am not sure why you would have received an error. Perhaps if you fix #2 above, it will work.

Chris
